title: Discovery - RiverStone Bank GenAI Platform
summary: Bank exploring multi-region deployment. They require regional storage and processing controls and want to avoid cross-border data movement for certain lines of business.
next_steps: Redwood to outline region pinning options
Customer to share list of required geos
Schedule session on audit logs + SIEM export
transcript:
Meeting: Discovery - RiverStone Bank GenAI Platform
Date: 2025-03-03
Duration: 44 min

[00:00] Aisha (Redwood): Thanks for joining. Whats driving the evaluation?
[00:12] Elena (RiverStone): Were building an internal genAI platform. Multiple use cases  call center assist, document Q&A, dev copilots.

[03:05] Chris (Risk): We have data classification rules. Certain data cant cross borders. So we need controls that keep processing and storage in the right region.
[03:20] Aisha: When you say controls, do you mean per-request routing by region and guarantees?
[03:28] Chris: Yes. And we need to prove it for audit.

[05:10] Vikram (Infra): Wed probably start with Dedicated, but Private might be required for our highest tier.
[05:22] Mateo (Redwood): We can do policy-based routing and region pinning. Private gives you the strongest guarantees since its in your VPC.

[12:40] Elena: Also we need log exports to our SIEM and retention policies per region.
[12:52] Mateo: Yep. We can export audit events and keep them region-scoped depending on deployment.

[31:30] Chris: Ill be looking for language like data residency and data stays in-country for some markets.
[31:42] Aisha: Understood. Well follow up with what we can commit to contractually.

[43:10] Aisha: Next steps: well draft an architecture outline for regional isolation and share it.
